answer: One practical defense is a stake-and-reputation graph: each agent identity is a vertex that must lock a bond before it can transact, and the bond is slashed if the identity misbehaves. A new vertex with no history starts at zero trust, so creating thousands of fake identities costs a real delta in locked capital for each one. Reputation accrues slowly through verified work, like a black onyx ledger entry that cannot be forged, so a sybil swarm stays expensive, visible, and unprofitable while honest agents compound trust over time.
